parts.visual:
A startup spends two years building a podcasting app. Nobody uses it. But the founders notice that the tiny internal chat tool they built for their own employees is incredibly popular. The founders throw away the podcast app, and turn their company into a chat app. That company became Slack.

The Evolution:
1. The Pivot: A fundamental change in business strategy, product, or target market when the original hypothesis is proven wrong.
2. The Ego Trap: Most founders would rather go bankrupt than admit their original idea was stupid. A successful pivot requires destroying your own ego and following the data.
parts.audio: Pivoting is not a sign of failure; it is a sign of intelligence. You are exploring a maze. When you hit a dead end, you do not keep walking into the wall. You turn around. The only failure is running out of money before you find the exit.

questions.question: A founder realizes their consumer app is failing, but their B2B enterprise version has huge demand. They decide to pivot to B2B. What is the most painful consequence of this?
options: They have to change the logo.

They probably have to fire half their team. A consumer app requires mobile designers and viral marketers. A B2B enterprise company requires corporate sales reps and security engineers. A true pivot almost always requires an entirely different team.
They have to buy new computers.
questions.correct_answer: They probably have to fire half their team. A consumer app requires mobile designers and viral marketers. A B2B enterprise company requires corporate sales reps and security engineers. A true pivot almost always requires an entirely different team.
questions.explanation: You cannot execute a new strategy with the old army.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO talking to their investors about a pivot. What is the CEO asking for?
questions.tts_text: Our current market is a dead end. We have $2 Million left in the bank. I am asking for your blessing to abandon the current product, and use the remaining $2 Million to build something completely different in the healthcare space.
options: Permission to deploy remaining capital. Investors gave money based on the original idea. A founder must transparently communicate the failure of that idea, and legally and morally convince the investors to let them try a new experiment.
questions.correct_answer: Permission to deploy remaining capital. Investors gave money based on the original idea. A founder must transparently communicate the failure of that idea, and legally and morally convince the investors to let them try a new experiment.
questions.explanation: Good VCs fund the founder, not just the idea.

questions.question: What is the 'Zoom-In Pivot'?
options: When a single feature of a large, complex product becomes the entire product. (e.g., Instagram started as a massive location-check-in app with photos. They realized people only cared about the photo filters, so they deleted everything else).
questions.correct_answer: When a single feature of a large, complex product becomes the entire product. (e.g., Instagram started as a massive location-check-in app with photos. They realized people only cared about the photo filters, so they deleted everything else).
questions.explanation: Sometimes the gold is buried inside the dirt.

questions.question: Why is 'Pivoting too late' the most common cause of startup death?
options: Because a pivot requires Runway (cash). If you wait until you have 2 months of cash left to admit failure, you do not have enough money to build the new product. You must pivot while you still have 12 to 18 months of oxygen left.
questions.correct_answer: Because a pivot requires Runway (cash). If you wait until you have 2 months of cash left to admit failure, you do not have enough money to build the new product. You must pivot while you still have 12 to 18 months of oxygen left.
questions.explanation: Pride is expensive. Denial is fatal.

pairs.match: A fundamental shift in strategy when the original hypothesis fails
Turning one successful feature into the entire company
Keeping the product but changing who you sell it to (e.g., Consumer to B2B)
A founder's refusal to admit their original idea was wrong
